title: How extreme rain is putting orangutans at risk
description:
Orangutans are the world’s most endangered apes and they’re now even closer to extinction. They live on two islands in southeast Asia: Sumatra and Borneo. In November, an extreme weather event in the area killed more than 1,000 people there, plus about 7% of the world’s rarest type of orangutan according to a new study.

BBC Climate and Science reporter Georgina Rannard takes us through how orangutans are being pushed towards extinction and what some countries and charities are doing to protect them.

We also hear from a conservationist making an effort to save the species.

summaryZh: 本集讨论紅毛猩猩（orangutan）的生存危机。BBC 報導指出，紅毛猩猩主要分布在 Sumatra 和 Borneo 的熱帶雨林與低地沼澤，栖息地因棕櫚油種植、採礦、伐木與水力發電等開發而被破壞與切割，導致族群愈來愈 isolated 並面臨法律及非法的捕捉與交易威脅。去年的極端氣候事件（四天強降雨與土石流）造成約 1,000 人死亡，也導致約 58 隻 Tapanuli 紅毛猩猩死亡，約為該物種總數的 約 7% ，使牠們更接近 extinction。報導也說明有保育工作在進行，例如保護棲地、人工繁殖計畫與國際間出資以換取不砍伐森林等策略，嘗試降低滅絕風險。
summaryEn: This episode explains how orangutans are at greater risk. They live mainly on Sumatra and Borneo in rainforests and swamps. Habitat loss from palm oil farming, mining, logging and hydropower is fragmenting populations. An extreme storm last November killed about 1,000 people and about 58 Tapanuli orangutans — roughly 7% of that species — pushing them closer to extinction. Conservation efforts include protected areas, breeding programs and payments to countries to keep forests standing.
